# Build Moodle course content

This skill drives a Moodle site through the MCP server of the plugin local_mcpcourse. It is a snapshot of the scenario plans of the plugin: the plan that the server returns is authoritative when they differ.

## How to work

1. Choose the scenario below that matches the request. Unsure? Call `scenario_catalog_get` and pick the slug there.
2. Call `scenario_get_plan {"slug": "<slug>"}` and follow the plan the server returns.
3. Ask only for the missing required inputs, and for sensitive people, grades, enrolments or destructive actions.
4. Go pre -> run -> check. Apply every guard before any write. Pass a `request_id` on every write: the same id makes a retry safe, and `undo` reverts the writes of the session.
5. Quote in the answer what the check tools return, not what you meant to do.
6. Always finish with `session_check` (no argument): it lists the writes of the session, the refusals that no success of the same tool followed and the grades saved without reading the submission. Fix each item or report it to the teacher.

The rule of every plan, as the server states it:

> Precedence: explicit user request > def. Entries prefixed "!" in def are locked defaults: override them only on an explicit user request plus confirmation. Apply pedago_rules unless the user explicitly opts out. Follow the order pre -> run -> check, and apply every guard before any write. End with check: call the check tools (they alone prove the result) and quote in the final answer what they return, not what you meant to do; if a check tool shows the result missing, say so. Last, call session_check: it lists the writes of this session, the refusals that no success of the same tool followed and the grades saved without reading the submission; fix each one or report it.

## Full course build (`course_full_build`)

- Goal: Build a complete course skeleton (sections, intro labels, resources, activities, final quiz) or extend a single section.
- Risk: medium
- Plan: `scenario_get_plan {"slug":"course_full_build"}`

Inputs to collect (a required input blocks until the teacher gives it):

- `courseid` (int, required) -> `courseid`
- `scope` (string, optional) -> `section`: full course (default) or one target section number
- `theme` (string, optional), informs drafting only: subject matter used to draft titles and content
- `level` (string, optional), informs drafting only: audience level (e.g. L1, M2, professional)
- `objectives` (string, optional), informs drafting only: learning objectives; drafted with the obj pack when absent
- `volume` (string, optional) -> `sections`: overrides the default of 4 sections

Defaults (a "!" entry is locked: change it only on an explicit request, after confirmation):

- 4 sections
- one intro label per section
- one resource per section
- one active activity per section
- final recap quiz

Steps:

1. Read first (pre): `course_get`, `course_sections_list`, `activity_list`
2. Write (run): `course_starter_bundle_create`
3. When needed (opt): `section_create`, `activity_create`, `quiz_create_with_questions`, `activity_completion_settings_update`, `workshop_get`, `image_draw_badge`, `badge_create_from_staged_file`
4. Prove the result (check): `course_get`, `course_sections_list`, `activity_list`
5. Close with `session_check`.

Guards, before any write:

- journal every write (request_id); undo reverts: course_starter_bundle_create, section_create, activity_create, badge_create_from_staged_file; no undo for: quiz_create_with_questions, activity_completion_settings_update
- confirm before writing into a non-empty course
- badge for a grade: set the pass mark of the activity BEFORE the criterion, with activity_completion_settings_update {cmid, completion: 2, completionusegrade: true, completionpassgrade: true, passinggrade: N} (quiz_update has no passinggrade), then badge_create_from_staged_file or badge_criteria_set with activity_completion [{cmid}]; the criterion is the completion of the activity, not a mark. Moodle only knows "at least N": tell the teacher that "more than 15" becomes "15 or more" (15 included). The badge stays inactive until activate_badge true, which awards it at once to everyone who already passed (notified, not undone by undo): ask the teacher, then name the holders with badge_recipients_list and quote them

Minimal call of each write (placeholder ids 42, 1234: replace the ids and the values, keep the names):

```text
course_starter_bundle_create {"courseid":42,"sections":[{"activities":["label","page","quiz:practice"]}]}
section_create {"courseid":42,"name":"Revision","summary":"<p>Revision materials</p>","visible":true}
activity_create {"courseid":2,"section":1,"module":"url","params":{"name":"Moodle Docs","externalurl":"https://docs.moodle.org"}}
quiz_create_with_questions {"courseid":42,"section":1,"category":{"name":"European capitals"},"quiz":{"name":"Capitals quiz","intro":"<p>Knowledge check quiz.</p>","attempts":1,"questionsperpage":1},"questions":[{"name":"France","qtype":"multichoice","questiontext":"What is the capital of France?","answers":[{"text":"Paris","fraction":1},{"text":"Lyon","fraction":0}],"page":1,"maxmark":1}]}
activity_completion_settings_update {"cmid":62,"completion":2,"completionposts":1}
image_draw_badge {"courseid":42}
badge_create_from_staged_file {"courseid":42,"uploadid":10,"name":"Example","course_completion":{"enabled":true}}
```

Done when: course_sections_list and activity_list show the targeted sections, each with an intro label, a resource and an active activity, plus the final quiz for full builds; the final answer quotes what they return.

## Lesson building (`lesson_build`)

- Goal: Build a lesson: create the lesson activity, then its content pages and question pages, and wire the jumps between them.
- Risk: medium
- Plan: `scenario_get_plan {"slug":"lesson_build"}`

Inputs to collect (a required input blocks until the teacher gives it):

- `courseid` (int, required) -> `courseid`
- `section` (int, optional) -> `section`
- `lesson` (int, optional) -> `cmid`: course module id of an existing lesson; without it a new lesson is created
- `pages` (object[], required) -> `qtype`, `title`, `contents`, `answers`: the pages in order: content or question (multichoice, truefalse, shortanswer, numerical, matching, essay), with answers, feedback and jumps
- `theme` (string, optional), informs drafting only: subject matter used to draft the pages

Defaults (a "!" entry is locked: change it only on an explicit request, after confirmation):

- create the lesson with activity_create (module lesson), then add the pages one by one in reading order
- a content page explains, then a question page checks it, with feedback on every answer
- create the page a jump aims at before the page that jumps to it, or fix the jump afterwards with lesson_page_update
- for a final quiz after the lesson (optional), create a quiz in the same section: quiz_create_with_questions, or activity_create (module quiz) when the questions come later

Steps:

1. Read first (pre): `course_get`, `course_sections_list`, `activity_list`, `lesson_pages_list?existing_lesson`
2. Write (run): `activity_create`, `lesson_page_create`
3. When needed (opt): `lesson_page_update?jumps_or_fixes`, `lesson_page_move?reorder`, `lesson_page_get`, `lesson_page_delete?after_confirm`, `quiz_create_with_questions?final_quiz`, `activity_completion_settings_update`
4. Prove the result (check): `lesson_pages_list`, `lesson_page_get`
5. Close with `session_check`.

Guards, before any write:

- journal every write (request_id); undo reverts: activity_create, lesson_page_create, lesson_page_update (title and contents), lesson_page_move; no undo for: quiz_create_with_questions
- lesson_page_delete is not undoable and removes the answers of students recorded on the page: confirm first
- confirm before changing a lesson that students already attempted

Consent (a site that asks for it, the default of a new site): lesson_page_delete: the first call that would write changes nothing and answers CONSENT_TICKET_NEEDED with error.consent (preview, consent_ticket, approve_url for a click). Compare the preview with the request: if it fits, send the same call with consent_ticket without asking again; if it differs, ask.

Minimal call of each write (placeholder ids 42, 1234: replace the ids and the values, keep the names):

```text
activity_create {"courseid":2,"section":1,"module":"url","params":{"name":"Moodle Docs","externalurl":"https://docs.moodle.org"}}
lesson_page_create {"cmid":1234,"qtype":"content","title":"Example","answers":[{"answer":"Continue","jumpto":"nextpage"}]}
lesson_page_create {"cmid":1234,"qtype":"multichoice","title":"Q1","contents":"<p>3/4 = ?</p>","answers":[{"answer":"0.75","response":"Right.","jumpto":"nextpage","score":1},{"answer":"0.34","response":"No.","jumpto":"thispage","score":0}]}
lesson_page_create {"cmid":1234,"qtype":"truefalse","title":"Q2","contents":"<p>1/2 = 0.5</p>","answers":[{"answer":"True","response":"Right.","jumpto":"nextpage","score":1},{"answer":"False","response":"No.","jumpto":"thispage","score":0}]}
lesson_page_create {"cmid":1234,"qtype":"shortanswer","title":"Q3","contents":"<p>Capital of France?</p>","answers":[{"answer":"Paris","response":"Right.","jumpto":"nextpage","score":1}],"other_answer":{"response":"No.","jumpto":"thispage","score":0}}
lesson_page_create {"cmid":1234,"qtype":"numerical","title":"Q4","contents":"<p>3/4 = ?</p>","answers":[{"answer":"0.75","response":"Right.","jumpto":"nextpage","score":1}],"other_answer":{"response":"No.","jumpto":"thispage","score":0}}
lesson_page_create {"cmid":1234,"qtype":"matching","title":"Q5","contents":"<p>Match each fraction.</p>","answers":[{"answer":"1/2","response":"0.5"},{"answer":"1/4","response":"0.25"}],"correct":{"response":"Right.","jumpto":"nextpage","score":1},"wrong":{"response":"No.","jumpto":"thispage","score":0}}
lesson_page_create {"cmid":1234,"qtype":"essay","title":"Q6","contents":"<p>Explain 3/4.</p>","answers":[{"jumpto":"nextpage","score":1}]}
lesson_page_move {"cmid":1234,"pageid":10,"afterpageid":10}

quiz_create_with_questions {"courseid":42,"section":1,"category":{"name":"European capitals"},"quiz":{"name":"Capitals quiz","intro":"<p>Knowledge check quiz.</p>","attempts":1,"questionsperpage":1},"questions":[{"name":"France","qtype":"multichoice","questiontext":"What is the capital of France?","answers":[{"text":"Paris","fraction":1},{"text":"Lyon","fraction":0}],"page":1,"maxmark":1}]}
activity_completion_settings_update {"cmid":62,"completion":2,"completionposts":1}
```

Done when: lesson_pages_list shows the pages in the agreed order, with the jumps wired to the intended pages.

## Fill a glossary (`glossary_populate`)

- Goal: Fill a glossary: create its categories, add the entries (concept, definition, aliases, categories) and approve those that wait for approval.
- Risk: medium
- Plan: `scenario_get_plan {"slug":"glossary_populate"}`

Inputs to collect (a required input blocks until the teacher gives it):

- `courseid` (int, required) -> `courseid`
- `glossary` (int, optional) -> `cmid`: course module id of the glossary; without it a new glossary is created
- `entries` (object[], required) -> `concept`, `definition`, `aliases`, `categoryids`: concepts with their definition, aliases and category
- `categories` (string[], optional) -> `name`: category names to create when missing

Defaults (a "!" entry is locked: change it only on an explicit request, after confirmation):

- list the categories and entries first: never add a concept that already exists
- to comment an entry (moderation note, remark) use entry_comment_add; comments must be open first: the site setting usecomments, and the glossary's allowcomments (activity_update, params.allowcomments true)
- create the categories before the entries that use them
- one concept per entry, a definition in plain HTML, aliases for the other names of the concept

Steps:

1. Read first (pre): `course_get`, `activity_list`, `glossary_categories_list`, `glossary_entries_list`
2. Write (run): `glossary_category_create?missing_category`, `glossary_entry_create`
3. When needed (opt): `activity_create?no_glossary`, `glossary_entry_approve?pending_entries`, `glossary_entry_update`, `glossary_category_update`, `glossary_entry_get`, `entry_comment_add?comment_requested`, `activity_update?open_comments`, `glossary_entry_delete?after_confirm`, `glossary_category_delete?after_confirm`
4. Prove the result (check): `glossary_entries_list`, `glossary_categories_list`
5. Close with `session_check`.

Guards, before any write:

- journal every write (request_id); undo reverts: glossary_category_create, glossary_entry_create, activity_create, glossary_entry_approve, glossary_entry_update, glossary_category_update, activity_update; no undo for: entry_comment_add
- an entry added by a person without mod/glossary:approve waits for approval: say so, and approve only when asked and allowed
- glossary_entry_delete and glossary_category_delete are not undoable: confirm first, and in bulk only after listing what goes

Consent (a site that asks for it, the default of a new site): glossary_entry_delete, glossary_category_delete: the first call that would write changes nothing and answers CONSENT_TICKET_NEEDED with error.consent (preview, consent_ticket, approve_url for a click). Compare the preview with the request: if it fits, send the same call with consent_ticket without asking again; if it differs, ask.

Minimal call of each write (placeholder ids 42, 1234: replace the ids and the values, keep the names):

```text
glossary_category_create {"cmid":1234,"name":"Example"}
glossary_entry_create {"cmid":1234,"concept":"example","definition":"example"}
activity_create {"courseid":2,"section":1,"module":"url","params":{"name":"Moodle Docs","externalurl":"https://docs.moodle.org"}}
glossary_entry_approve {"cmid":1234,"entryid":10,"approve":true}
entry_comment_add {"cmid":1234,"entryid":10,"content":"Example text"}
activity_update {"cmid":5,"params":{"name":"Updated Activity Name"}}
glossary_entry_delete {"cmid":1234,"entryid":10}
glossary_category_delete {"cmid":1234,"categoryid":3}
```

Done when: glossary_entries_list shows every agreed concept, in the agreed category, with its approval state said.

## Write in a wiki (`wiki_authoring`)

- Goal: Write in a wiki: find the right subwiki, create a page, or save a new version of a page without overwriting someone else.
- Risk: medium
- Plan: `scenario_get_plan {"slug":"wiki_authoring"}`

Inputs to collect (a required input blocks until the teacher gives it):

- `courseid` (int, required) -> `courseid`
- `wiki` (int, optional) -> `cmid`: course module id of the wiki; without it a new wiki is created
- `subwiki` (int, optional) -> `subwikiid`, `groupid`, `userid`: subwiki from wiki_subwikis_list; default: the one of the caller
- `title` (string, required) -> `title`
- `content` (string, required) -> `content`

Defaults (a "!" entry is locked: change it only on an explicit request, after confirmation):

- pick the subwiki first (one per group or per person in some wikis): pass its subwikiid
- write in the format of the wiki (html, creole or nwiki), the one wiki_page_get shows
- read the page with wiki_page_get right before saving, and send back the version read

Steps:

1. Read first (pre): `course_get`, `activity_list`, `wiki_subwikis_list`, `wiki_pages_list`
2. Write (run): `wiki_page_create`, `wiki_page_get`, `wiki_page_update`
3. When needed (opt): `activity_create?no_wiki`, `wiki_page_versions_list`
4. Prove the result (check): `wiki_pages_list`, `wiki_page_get`, `wiki_page_versions_list`
5. Close with `session_check`.

Guards, before any write:

- journal every write (request_id); undo reverts: wiki_page_update (the saved version), activity_create; no undo for: wiki_page_create
- wrongversionsave: the page changed since it was read; read it again, merge the new content with the changes of the other person, never force the old text back
- pageislocked: another person is editing the page; tell the teacher and retry later, do not loop

Minimal call of each write (placeholder ids 42, 1234: replace the ids and the values, keep the names):

```text
wiki_page_create {"cmid":1234,"title":"Example"}
wiki_page_update {"cmid":1234,"pageid":10,"content":"Example text","version":1}
activity_create {"courseid":2,"section":1,"module":"url","params":{"name":"Moodle Docs","externalurl":"https://docs.moodle.org"}}
```

Done when: wiki_page_get shows the new content at the next version, and wiki_page_versions_list lists the save.

## Build a database (`database_build`)

- Goal: Build a database activity: define its fields, then add the first entries, and approve the entries that wait for approval.
- Risk: medium
- Plan: `scenario_get_plan {"slug":"database_build"}`

Inputs to collect (a required input blocks until the teacher gives it):

- `courseid` (int, required) -> `courseid`
- `database` (cmid, optional) -> `cmid`: course module id of the database; without it a new one is created (activity_create, module data)
- `fields` (object[], required) -> `type`, `name`, `description`, `required`, `options`: name and type of each field (text, textarea, number, date, menu, radiobutton, checkbox, url...)
- `entries` (object[], optional) -> `values`

Defaults (a "!" entry is locked: change it only on an explicit request, after confirmation):

- the fields first (data_field_create, one per call): an entry holds only the fields that exist
- an entry gives a value per field name (values), as data_fields_list names them
- the templates of the database follow its fields: no template to write

Steps:

1. Read first (pre): `course_get`, `activity_list`, `data_fields_list?existing_database`
2. Write (run): `data_field_create`, `data_entry_create`
3. When needed (opt): `activity_create?no_database`, `data_field_update`, `data_entries_list`, `data_entry_approve?pending_entries`, `data_field_delete?after_confirm`
4. Prove the result (check): `data_fields_list`, `data_entries_list`
5. Close with `session_check`.

Guards, before any write:

- journal every write (request_id); undo reverts: data_field_create, data_entry_create, activity_create, data_field_update, data_entry_approve
- data_field_delete is not undoable and deletes the values of that field in every entry: confirm first
- an entry added by a person without mod/data:approve waits for approval: say so

Consent (a site that asks for it, the default of a new site): data_field_delete: the first call that would write changes nothing and answers CONSENT_TICKET_NEEDED with error.consent (preview, consent_ticket, approve_url for a click). Compare the preview with the request: if it fits, send the same call with consent_ticket without asking again; if it differs, ask.

Minimal call of each write (placeholder ids 42, 1234: replace the ids and the values, keep the names):

```text
data_field_create {"cmid":1234,"type":"text","name":"Example"}
data_entry_create {"cmid":1234,"values":[{"name":"Title","value":"Wind turbine"},{"fieldid":21,"value":"2026-06-01"}]}
activity_create {"courseid":2,"section":1,"module":"url","params":{"name":"Moodle Docs","externalurl":"https://docs.moodle.org"}}
data_entry_approve {"cmid":1234,"entryid":10,"approve":true}

```

Done when: data_fields_list shows the agreed fields and data_entries_list the entries, with their approval state said.

## Publish a SCORM package (`scorm_publish`)

- Goal: Publish a SCORM package as an activity: stage the zip in the course, create the SCORM activity from it, and read back how it is set.
- Risk: low
- Plan: `scenario_get_plan {"slug":"scorm_publish"}`

Inputs to collect (a required input blocks until the teacher gives it):

- `courseid` (int, required) -> `courseid`
- `section` (int, required) -> `section`
- `package` (file, required) -> `params.uploadid`: the SCORM .zip, staged with staged_file_add (its uploadid)
- `name` (string, required) -> `params.name`

Defaults (a "!" entry is locked: change it only on an explicit request, after confirmation):

- stage the .zip first (staged_file_add), then activity_create module scorm with params.uploadid
- activity_update changes the settings (grading, attempts, display), never the package: a new package is a new activity

Steps:

1. Read first (pre): `course_get`, `course_sections_list`, `staged_files_list?already_staged`
2. Write (run): `staged_file_add`, `activity_create`
3. When needed (opt): `activity_update?settings`, `activity_completion_settings_update`, `scorm_attempts_list?later`
4. Prove the result (check): `scorm_get`
5. Close with `session_check`.

Guards, before any write:

- journal every write (request_id); undo reverts: activity_create, activity_update; no undo for: activity_completion_settings_update
- a package that Moodle cannot read is refused with its reason: report it, do not retry with the same file

Minimal call of each write (placeholder ids 42, 1234: replace the ids and the values, keep the names):

```text
staged_file_add {"courseid":42,"file":{"download_url":"https://temporary-file-download-url.example/guide.pdf","file_id":"file_abc123","mime_type":"application/pdf","file_name":"guide.pdf"},"filedescription":"Learner guide PDF","purpose":"course_resource","dedupe_strategy":"unique","request_id":"agent-upload-file-42-001"}
activity_create {"courseid":2,"section":1,"module":"url","params":{"name":"Moodle Docs","externalurl":"https://docs.moodle.org"}}
activity_update {"cmid":5,"params":{"name":"Updated Activity Name"}}
activity_completion_settings_update {"cmid":62,"completion":2,"completionposts":1}
```

Done when: scorm_get shows the activity with the package, its version and its settings.

## Pedagogical rules

Apply the packs that a plan names (its `pedago` list) unless the teacher explicitly opts out:

- `align`: Constructive alignment: every activity and assessment item maps to one objective and its Bloom level; the assessment's cognitive level equals the objective's level; no orphan assessment.
- `fb`: Formative feedback is immediate and explanatory (why right/wrong), per item; summative feedback is deferred.
- `mcq`: MCQ rules: the stem is a complete, unambiguous question; exactly one correct answer; 3-4 plausible distractors drawn from frequent mistakes; homogeneous options; no "all/none of the above"; no grammatical cue; capitalize negations.
- `obj`: Objectives use the ABCD pattern (audience, observable behaviour, condition, degree) with an explicit Bloom verb; measurable; 3-6 per course, 1-2 per section; ban vague verbs like "know" or "understand".
- `struct`: Section sequence: intro -> objectives -> input -> active practice -> assessment; at least one objective and one active activity per section (never resources only); segment content to limit cognitive load.

## Finish: verify with session_check

Call `session_check {}` at the end of every task, even a read-only one, and report what it lists.
